Answer: B
Reason: The radiographic combination of a tubular opacity (representing a bronchocele or mucocoele) and an adjacent hyperlucent area (representing collateral air drift/hyperinflation) in the left upper lobe is the classic presentation of congenital bronchial atresia. This distinguishes it from infectious, neoplastic, or vascular etiologies which do not typically present with this specific paired finding.
